quiz.title: Data Ingestion Methods
quiz.description: Approaches to bringing data into a pipeline or platform, including batch ingestion, streaming ingestion, APIs, change data capture, and file-based ingestion.

questions.option_a: Collecting and loading data in large chunks at scheduled intervals
questions.option_b: Processing each record the instant it is created
questions.correct_answer: Collecting and loading data in large chunks at scheduled intervals

questions.option_a: Continuously ingesting data as individual events arrive, in near real time
questions.option_c: Manually copying files with a USB drive
questions.correct_answer: Continuously ingesting data as individual events arrive, in near real time

questions.option_a: A technique for identifying and capturing changes made to source data so they can be propagated downstream
questions.option_c: A way to encrypt a database
questions.correct_answer: A technique for identifying and capturing changes made to source data so they can be propagated downstream

questions.question_text: Which of these is a common way to ingest data from a third-party service?
questions.option_c: Manually retyping data from a screen

questions.question_text: What is a common challenge with real-time/streaming ingestion compared to batch?
questions.option_a: Handling out-of-order or late-arriving events and maintaining low latency
questions.option_b: It is always simpler to implement than batch
questions.option_d: It cannot handle any volume of data
questions.correct_answer: Handling out-of-order or late-arriving events and maintaining low latency

questions.question_text: What role does a message queue or event streaming platform, like Kafka, typically play in ingestion?
questions.option_a: Buffering and delivering events reliably between producers and consumers
questions.correct_answer: Buffering and delivering events reliably between producers and consumers

questions.question_text: What is 'polling' in the context of data ingestion?
questions.option_a: Repeatedly checking a source at intervals to see if new data is available
questions.option_b: A method of encrypting data at rest
questions.option_c: A way to visualize data on a dashboard
questions.correct_answer: Repeatedly checking a source at intervals to see if new data is available

questions.question_text: What is a webhook, in the context of ingesting data?
questions.option_a: An HTTP callback that a source system sends automatically when an event happens
questions.correct_answer: An HTTP callback that a source system sends automatically when an event happens

questions.question_text: Why might an organization choose a hybrid ingestion approach combining batch and streaming (sometimes called Lambda or Kappa architecture)?
questions.option_a: To balance the need for both historical, high-volume processing and low-latency, real-time updates
questions.option_b: Because streaming is illegal in most countries
questions.option_c: Because batch processing has been deprecated
questions.option_d: Because only one ingestion method is ever allowed
questions.correct_answer: To balance the need for both historical, high-volume processing and low-latency, real-time updates

questions.question_text: What is a common risk when ingesting data directly from production databases without care?
questions.option_a: Placing excessive load on the production system, affecting application performance
questions.option_c: Guaranteeing zero data loss with no design effort
questions.correct_answer: Placing excessive load on the production system, affecting application performance
